themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 141 THIS WEEK versus 84.2-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (67% increase, z-score 3.93), suggesting new or intensifying venues, construction, or events in Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: 141 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 84.2 weekly baseline (8-week average), z-score 3.93
67% spike in one week indicates acute, not gradual, change in commercial activity or compliance
Noise - Commercial is already #4 complaint category by volume (1,142 over 90 days), now accelerating further
reporting_angles: Which venues or construction projects ramped up operations this past week? Interview affected residents on specific blocks.
Has NYPD or 311 enforcement increased? Request complaint hotspot map and response times from NYPD noise unit.

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees & Tree Request Explosion
themes_detail.summary: New tree requests skyrocketed 2300% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average, z-score 8.69), concurrent with dead/dying tree complaints up 167% THIS WEEK (6 vs. 2.2 average), signaling either a sudden tree-health crisis or organized community effort to address canopy loss.
evidence: New Tree Request complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score 8.69, highest spike in dataset)
Dead/Dying Tree complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (167% increase, z-score 5.67)
Dual spike suggests either environmental stressor (disease, drought) or resident mobilization around greening
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks about recent tree deaths—disease, pests, or infrastructure damage? Request data on which streets are affected.
Is a community group or elected official leading a tree-planting campaign? Timing of 2300% spike suggests organized action, not random complaints.

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs & Animal Abuse Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped 500% LAST WEEK (6 vs. 1.0 average, z-score 4.47) and animal abuse reports rose 167% LAST WEEK (9 vs. 3.4 average, z-score 3.99), together suggesting either a dangerous dog problem or broader animal welfare crisis in the district.
evidence: Unleashed Dog complaints: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score 4.47)
Animal Abuse complaints: 9 LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average (167% increase, z-score 3.99)
Two separate but concurrent spikes in animal-related complaints suggest systemic issue, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Have there been attacks or aggressive incidents in parks (like McGolrick or Transmitter)? Interview NYPD or Animal Care & Control about enforcement.
Are shelters or rescues reporting intake surges? Link to potential hoarding, neglect, or abuse networks in the district.

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs & Wayfinding Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sign missing complaints surged 336% TWO WEEKS AGO (6 vs. 1.4 average, z-score 4.66), indicating systematic removal or degradation that may affect pedestrian safety and navigation, especially in a dense, rapidly changing neighborhood.
evidence: Street Sign - Missing complaints: 6 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% increase, z-score 4.66)
Spike has slightly faded since peak 2 weeks ago, but remains elevated signal of infrastructure neglect
Aligns with long-standing community board budget request for 'traffic and pedestrian safety, including traffic calming' improvements
reporting_angles: Map which streets and intersections are missing signs—is it localized or district-wide? Request DOT complaint hotspot data.
Has construction or development removed temporary signage that wasn't replaced? Connect to ULURP applications (200 Kent, 20 Berry, Monitor Point).

themes_detail.label: Spike in Building Inspections & Violations
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints surged 154% LAST WEEK (7 vs. 2.8 average, z-score 3.9), alongside 1,343 DOB permit filings in 90 days (215 new buildings, 40 demolitions), suggesting intense construction activity and rising resident complaints about inspection delays or violations.
evidence: SPIT complaints: 7 LAST WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (154% increase, z-score 3.9)
DOB permit filings: 1,343 in 90 days; 755 alterations + 215 new buildings indicate sustained heavy construction
Community board's repeated budget request for 'Other expense request for DOB' signals ongoing enforcement/inspection capacity gap
reporting_angles: Are inspections falling behind? Request DOB data on average inspection wait times and complaint resolution rates in this district.
Interview residents near major ULURP sites (200 Kent, 20 Berry, Monitor Point) about construction noise, safety barriers, and inspector presence.
